title: Message ids the ported simulation can emit that have no resolvable string today
policy: This file is a debt ledger, not a permission slip. The drift test (tools/i18n-port/verify-i18n-port.mjs) fails when the observed unresolved set differs from these entries in ANY direction:
- an id that is not resolvable and is not listed here  -> FAIL (a new unsolvable id reached the screen)
- an id that is listed here but is resolvable now      -> FAIL (stale entry: delete it and let the test prove the fix)
- a listed category that no longer matches             -> FAIL
Every entry carries the reference behaviour it deviates from and a fix path. Nothing here may be 'fixed' by editing js/** (frozen reference) or godot/src/sim/** (another owner's allowlist).

rc1-id-concatenation.what: godot/src/sim/sim.gd:2034 and :2038 build a message id by concatenating one id with a literal suffix ('%s secondServe' % reason) or by lowercasing an id ('doubleFault:%s' % reason.to_lower()). Neither result is a key of js/i18n.js.
rc1-id-concatenation.reference: js/game.js:2123 and :2128 render at emit time: `addEvent(state, `${reason} ${t("secondServeSuffix")}`)` and `scorePoint(..., t("doubleFault", { reason: reason.toLowerCase() }), ...)`, where `reason` is already the call site's `t("serveOutBox")` / `t("serveWallFault")`.
rc1-id-concatenation.whyItsNotMine: the fix is a sim-side encoding change (carry the suffix key as a separate field or a params dictionary instead of concatenating strings) and godot/src/sim/** is outside this task's write allowlist.
rc1-id-concatenation.fixPath: sim owner: replace the concatenation with `add_event(state, reason)` plus a declared params carrier, then bind the suffix through a `secondServeSuffix` param rule in locale_rules.json. The drift test will require the ledger entry to be deleted in the same change.

rc2-lost-parameters.what: godot/src/sim/sim.gd:782 and :805 store the bare id `serveHint`. Its value is `"{ordinal} di servizio dal basso{suffix}: cerca il diagonale."`, and the port's event stream carries neither parameter, so resolving it prints the braces.
rc2-lost-parameters.reference: js/game.js:2629-2632 and :2657-2660 render `t("serveHint", { ordinal: t(state.serveAttempts ? "serveOrdSecond" : "serveOrdFirst"), suffix: input.slice ? t("serveSliceSuffix") : "" })` at emit time.
rc2-lost-parameters.whyItsNotMine: supplying the parameters means changing what the sim stores (a params dictionary alongside the id); godot/src/sim/** is outside this task's write allowlist. Inventing a default ordinal would be fabricating match state.
rc2-lost-parameters.fixPath: sim owner: store `{ id: "serveHint", params: { ordinal: ..., suffix: ... } }`; locale.gd already accepts a params dictionary.

rc3-reference-hardcoded-literal.what: godot/src/sim/sim.gd:2045 sets `state.pointMessage = "LET"`. Per the port's own boundary rule the sim may not store rendered text, so it stores a short literal; the reference's let message is the hardcoded string "LET · Servizio da ripetere".
rc3-reference-hardcoded-literal.reference: js/game.js:2135 — `state.pointMessage = "LET · Servizio da ripetere";` is a literal, not a `t()` call: this one string is not translatable in the reference either. Note the sentence "Servizio da ripetere" does exist, inside the value of the key `evLet`.
rc3-reference-hardcoded-literal.whyItsNotMine: adding a new key to the reference string table is a product decision for Luca (the port must not invent strings the reference does not have), and editing js/** is forbidden.
rc3-reference-hardcoded-literal.fixPath: open human decision: either accept the reference's own untranslated literal in the port, or add a `pointLet` key to the reference table (and then re-freeze the baseline) — record the choice in the locale contract, do not machine-invent it.

yes — same path, the ball hit the glass before the bounce
yes — `score_point` awards the point to the opponent, so the prefix is `pointOpp`
no — a double fault always scores for `State.other(state.serveSide)`; kept because the id is derivable from the source and an unreachable unresolvable id is still a latent trap
